evals.prompt: I want to order 100 bacterial-phage designs from the selected RL checkpoint. Decide how many sequences to generate, deduplicate them at 99%, apply all approved QC, and rank the final candidates if defensible.
evals.expected_output: An adaptive rollout plan driven by a compatible pilot, conservative post-QC yield, saturation, and the requested order count rather than a fixed large generation count.
assertions: The response runs or reuses a compatible 1,000-design pilot with identical checkpoint, prompts, sampling, canonicalization, filters, tools, and clustering profile before forecasting yield.
The response estimates conservative post-hard-QC and post-99%-cluster yield with uncertainty and monitors accumulation and saturation across additional 1,000-design batches.
The response targets roughly three times the order count when meaningful ranking exists or 1.25 times otherwise, stopping for reserve, saturation, or budget and asking before expensive scaling.
The response does not use the historical 358/1000 result as a universal forecast and does not hard-code 10,000 generations for a 100-order request.
The response ranks only passing unique representatives with predeclared defensible scores and never lets ranking override hard QC or uniqueness.

evals.prompt: Generate a 1,000-design proof-of-concept rollout. Filters 1 through 6, 8, and 9 are mandatory; another requirement can pass through either route A or route B. Produce an auditable final manifest.
evals.expected_output: A deterministic generation, canonicalization, deduplication, nested all/any QC, clustering, and reporting pipeline.
assertions: The response freezes checkpoint and SFT/prompt lineage, sampling, seeds, objective/filter versions, tools/models, and source/config hashes before generation.
The response validates sequences, applies topology-aware canonicalization, exact-deduplicates before expensive tools, and preserves raw-to-representative mapping.
The response represents filters 1-6, 8, and 9 as mandatory hard all and the route choice as a nested hard any, with mandatory missing data or tool failure failing closed.
The response records per-filter waterfall, route overlap and dominance, then clusters passers at 99% identity with declared coverage semantics.
The response writes ordered intent-named scripts plus raw, canonical, exact-deduplicated, QC-passing, cluster-representative, ranked, rejected, provenance, and summary artifacts.
The response reports the proof-of-concept counts without silently adding filter 7 or conflating them with a different historical profile.

evals.prompt: Generate and filter final designs from the selected RL checkpoint on the GPUs assigned to this host. Use the fastest qualified Evo2 vLLM setup, and leave an auditable command and result bundle for another operator.
evals.expected_output: A host-verified selected-checkpoint export, capacity-qualified multi-GPU vLLM rollout, strict output validation, QC pipeline, and provenance-complete report.
assertions: The response builds and sources the recipe environment on the actual execution host and verifies Python, package/plugin, vLLM, entry-point, and CUDA visibility before generation.

The response exports the exact selected post-RL MBridge checkpoint to a fresh vLLM safetensors directory and records the source inventory plus config, index, manifest, and shard hashes; it never silently reuses a base-policy export.

The response gives executable ./ci_build.sh and .ci_test_env.sh setup followed by public evo2_export_mbridge_to_vllm and infer_evo2 commands that bind --model, --rl-checkpoint, --rl-tokenizer-json, and the frozen --prompt-file.

The response identifies TP2 MP+async O2/balanced, compilation mode 3, and exact-batch FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs as the measured two-H100 reference while permitting a correctness- and capacity-qualified higher TP or disjoint DP engine groups on larger allocations.

The generation command uses adaptive --tensor-parallel-size auto plus the qualified --optimization-level 2, --performance-mode balanced, and --async-scheduling defaults, while capacity-testing physical batch and capture sizes for the assigned system.
The response uses every assigned GPU without device overlap, binds real local wave sizes into capture configuration, and gives disjoint request and seed partitions to multiple engine groups.

The response requires exact output lengths, allowed DNA symbols with no EOS, finite aligned chosen logprobs, and unique advancing request seeds before canonicalization, deduplication, hard QC, clustering, and ranking.
The response saves executable export and generation commands, resolved config, source and runtime hashes, raw rows, rejection reasons, QC waterfall, unique passing representatives, and final summary.
